conviction_note: The Q3 macro ran well above Eni's own July scenario: Brent $97 vs $85, TTF about EUR63/MWh vs EUR50, and European refining margins at records. Eni's published policy pays 100% of the incremental CFFO above $90 Brent or above the refining trigger as an extraordinary dividend, and that decision is due 'in October'. This stock has risen on each of its last three prints on distribution news (Q2 2026 +4.5% intraday Milan). That gives a modest long lean. It is held to p_up 56 because the street already expects a special dividend of about EUR1bn and FY CFFO of about EUR16bn (Equita), the stock is at its 52-week high after +7.6% over 20 days, and the quarter itself screens in line (bar EUR2.48-2.6bn adjusted net). The findings sum to +0.8 and the scaled number is +0.34. The two are not fitted to each other; the gap is the run-up and the distribution expectations already in the price.

The line the stock has traded on is shareholder returns, and the street expectation there is a special dividend of about EUR1bn plus FY CFFO of about EUR16bn against a EUR15bn guide (Equita, via finanzaonline, https://www.finanzaonline.com/?p=786277, undated snippet, 403 on fetch).

findings.finding: Every Q3 2026 scenario input printed above the FY scenario Eni used on 29 July to set its EUR15bn CFFO guide and EUR3.4bn buyback (Brent $85, SERM $14, TTF EUR50/MWh): Brent averaged $97.0, TTF averaged $21.5/MMBtu (about EUR63/MWh), and TotalEnergies' European refining marker was $33.2/b against $13.5 in Q2. Brent was still around $100 in mid-October. Eni's published policy pays 100% of the CFFO increment as an extraordinary dividend in Q4 when Brent is above $90 or refining margins are 50%+ above budget, with the decision due 'in October'. Using Eni's own sensitivities (EUR0.11bn per $1 Brent, EUR0.08bn per $1 SERM), FY Brent near $95 and FY SERM near $13-15 give an increment of roughly EUR1.1-1.4bn. The street expects about EUR1bn (Equita) and FY CFFO of about EUR16bn. The Plenitude deconsolidation (completed 1 October) and the $2bn Ares capital expected in Q3 also push gearing below the 10% floor, which supports a buyback upsize on top.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Distribution news has driven the last three prints. Q3 2025: shares rose on a buyback upsize (https://sweetcrudereports.com/eni-ups-buyback-on-strong-q3-results-shares-rise/). Q1 2026: about +1% despite an earnings miss, because the buyback rose to EUR2.8bn (https://www.milanofinanza.it/news/eni-gli-analisti-conti-sotto-le-attese-ma-convincono-il-buyback-a-2-8-miliardi-e-le-stime-sulla-202604241117072364). Q2 2026: +4.5% intraday Milan on an 11% beat plus a buyback raise to EUR3.4bn (https://quifinanza.it/economia/finanza/eni-vola-borsa-trimestrale-utile-buyback-dividendo-2026/1010238/). The baseline's own 8-move history is monthly 6-K noise and was not used.
findings.why_not_priced: The direction is partly priced: the stock is at its 52-week high, +7.6% over 20 days, and Equita's EUR1bn special is in circulation. What is not visibly priced is the size of the special. Money.it's widely read calculation (2026-10-06) puts it at EUR640m, counting only the SERM leg at the July $14 scenario. Applying the policy's Brent-above-$90 leg to the realised Q3 tape adds about EUR0.4-0.6bn. If the market had priced EUR1.2bn+, the preview pieces would quote it rather than EUR0.64-1bn. The risk is the other way too: Eni may pay only part now and defer the rest as 'depending on how long the scenario lasts'.

findings.finding: Peer updates point to a large sequential refining step-up for Eni's Q3. TotalEnergies' European refining marker went from $13.5 to $33.2/b (+146%), with R&C cash flow guided about $2bn higher QoQ, and Shell put Q3 refining margins at a record $42 vs $24. Eni's Q2 SERM was $8.3/b, which earned refining EBIT of EUR80m. Scaling by the peer marker implies a Q3 SERM near $20, worth roughly +EUR0.2bn of quarterly refining EBIT (EUR0.02bn per $1 per quarter). That roughly offsets the Brent drop ($104.5 to $97, about -EUR0.2bn quarterly CFFO), and higher TTF (+EUR0.1bn) is upside to GGP. The Q3 adjusted net bridge from Q2's EUR2.33bn therefore lands around EUR2.45-2.55bn, at or slightly above the EUR2.48bn company consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat consensus by about 11% and the stock rose +4.5% intraday, with the buyback raised the same day. Q1 2026 missed by about 14% (1.3 vs 1.51 per WallStreetItalia) and still rose about 1% on the buyback. The quarter's number has mattered less than distributions.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. BofA notes that the majors' Q3 trading updates lifted sector estimates about 5%, and the company-compiled EUR2.48bn is above Q2's EUR2.33bn. The residual upside is that Eni's refining is small and was loss-making a year ago, so consensus models may under-scale the SERM jump. If fully priced, the company consensus would sit nearer EUR2.6bn (where VA already is).
findings.independence: Proxy. It shares the TotalEnergies and Shell series with the capital-return finding above. Eni itself has published no Q3 SERM. The Shell Q3 update is the independent confirmation of the margin step-up (https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/stock-market-news/company--news/shell-sees-record-q3-refining-margins,-lifts-gas-production-estimate).

findings.finding: BofA (2026-10-16) sits below Visible Alpha consensus on Eni's Q3: adjusted net EUR2.5bn vs EUR2.6bn (-3%), adjusted EBIT EUR3.5bn vs EUR3.8bn (-8%, flat QoQ). BofA attributes the EBIT gap mostly to the Searah JV (Indonesia/Malaysia, with Petronas) no longer contributing to consolidated EBIT. Any wire headline comparing consolidated EBIT with an un-updated consensus could therefore read as a miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior on a perimeter-driven EBIT miss. Q1 2026's headline miss was bought on the buyback (about +1%).
findings.why_not_priced: The VA consensus at EUR2.6bn sits above the company's own EUR2.48bn, so part of the street carries a higher net bar than the company-compiled one. A print near EUR2.5bn reads as in line against Eni's consensus and as a slight miss against VA. Which bar the wires use on the day is not knowable in advance. BofA still raised its target (to EUR24.5, below spot of about EUR26.1), so it is not a negative call.
findings.independence: None. This is a single-bank read. Eni's own Q2 release confirms that Searah was set up in Q2 as a 50/50 JV (equity-accounted), which supports the perimeter mechanism (https://www.eni.com/content/dam/enicom/documents/press-release/migrated/2026-it/07/CS-risultati-secondo-trimestre-2026.pdf).
